                                    BOARD AGENDA ITEM 4a

TO:                         Board of Directors

FROM:                       Chris Skelly, Information Technology Manager

MEETING DATE:               October 15, 2026

ITEM – PROJECT NAME:        Environmental Science Research Institute Geographic
                            Information System Small Utility Enterprise License Agreement
                            Renewal

REQUESTED BOARD ACTION: Authorize staff to renew the Small Utility Enterprise License
Agreement for three additional years with the Environmental Science Research Institute
for access to the ESRI term license software in the amount of $112,800.

DISCUSSION: As indicated in the attached proposed contract from Environmental
Science Research Institute (ESRI), the annual cost for the Small Utility Enterprise License
Agreement (SUELA) will be $37,600 per year, for a total Contract value of $112,800 over
a three-year term. The agreement will be billed annually.

The SUELA provides the District with enterprise access to ESRI Geographic Information
System (GIS) software and licensing needed to support District operations. This licensing
model has enabled staff to expand GIS editing capabilities, improve the accuracy and
availability of maps for field staff and inspectors, and develop web-based GIS tools for
District-wide use. Tablet-based GIS applications allow crews to access GIS information in
the field and integrate with the District’s Nexgen Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
application. The agreement also supports the continued development of customer-
facing interactive maps for water outages, project status, and other timely District
information.

The annual cost is included in and will be funded through the Fiscal Year 2029
Information Technology Service Contracts budget. As a renewal of the District’s existing
ESRI Enterprise Licensing Agreement, the SUELA maintains continuity for District GIS
systems, staff workflows, field applications, and public-facing mapping services.

Staff recommends that the Board authorize staff to renew the Small Utility Enterprise
License Agreement with ESRI for an additional three-year term, at a total cost not to
exceed $112,800, for continued access to ESRI term-license software and related GIS
capabilities.

                                   BOARD AGENDA ITEM 4b


TO:                         Board of Directors

FROM:                       Greg Dupree, Accounting Manager

MEETING DATE:               October 15, 2026

ITEM – PROJECT NAME:        Establish District Software Subscription-Based Information
                            Technology Arrangement Capitalization Policy

REQUESTED BOARD ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 3346-26 in accordance with
Governmental Accounting Standards Board Statement No. 96, to establish District
software subscription-based information technology arrangement capitalization policy.

DISCUSSION: The purpose of this Policy is to establish accounting and reporting
procedures for Subscription-Based Information Technology Arrangements (SBITAs) in
accordance with Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) Statement No.
96. The policy is intended to ensure consistent application of capitalization requirements
while balancing the administrative effort associated with recording and tracking SBITAs.
The District currently reports subscription assets and liabilities associated with software
arrangements in our financial statements. Beginning in Fiscal Year 2027, The District will
set its capitalization requirement for these arrangements at $100,000. SBITAs that do not
meet the capitalization threshold shall be recorded as expenditures or expenses in the
period incurred.

TO:                         Board of Directors

FROM:                       Sara Nelson, Customer Service Supervisor

MEETING DATE:               October 15, 2026

ITEM – PROJECT NAME:        Cash Rounding Authorization

REQUESTED BOARD ACTION: Approve Resolution No. 3347-26, authorizing the rounding
of certain cash payments to the nearest five cents and establishing related
administrative procedures.

DISCUSSION: Following the United States Mint’s cessation of the production of one-cent
coins and the reduced availability of pennies, it is necessary that the District implement
a cash rounding practice for customer payments made wholly or partly in cash. That
proposed would allow the District, to the extent permitted by California law, to round
cash-payment amounts to the nearest five cents when exact change is unavailable or
impractical, while preserving the exact underlying amount of each District bill, rate, fee,
charge, deposit, penalty, or other obligation. Any rounding difference would be
recorded as a small credit or balance on the applicable customer account and would
not independently result in late fees, collection activity, shutoff notices, or other adverse
account action. Resolution No. 3347-26 also authorizes the General Manager or
designee to establish administrative procedures for system configuration, cashier
reconciliation, customer communications, internal controls, and periodic monitoring,
with implementation occurring after required staff training, customer notice, and system
updates are complete.

                                 BOARD AGENDA ITEM 6c

TO:                         Board of Directors

FROM:                       Laura Hendrickson, Associate Engineer

MEETING DATE:               October 15, 2026

ITEM – PROJECT NAME:        2026 Water Meter Installation Project

REQUESTED BOARD ACTION: 1) Approve Change Order No. 2 to White Rock
Construction, Inc. in the amount of $28,137.76; and 2) Authorize the Acting General
Manager to execute Change Order No. 2.

DISCUSSION: The 2026 Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) Water Meter Installation
Project began construction on July 7, 2026. The Project will install meters at seventy-two
(72) remaining residential properties within the District’s service area that do not
currently have meters, the majority of which are located in the Loop Road area. The
remaining 72 properties were previously skipped due to various difficulties with locating
or accessing the services.

The majority of this Change Order, totaling $23,674.28, is for Time-and-Materials (T&M)
work to locate previously unidentified water services at 1685 Choctaw Street, 1411 June
Way, and 2209 Chiapa Drive. These services could not be located due to inaccurate or
incomplete records and the lack of visible features that could be used to identify their
locations. District staff and the contractor initially attempted to locate the services using
traditional methods, including the use of a thumper. While the thumper was helpful in
narrowing down the potential locations, additional investigation and excavation were
required to locate the services. Two of the three services have been located and
meters have been installed at those properties.

Separately, an unmarked sewer lateral was encountered and damaged during
construction, requiring repairs totaling $3,829.21. The lateral was not identified in
available records and was part of a previously unknown configuration in which multiple
individual laterals connect to a common “main” lateral. The Change Order also
includes $634.27 to relocate a water meter to the District’s side of a customer shutoff
valve.

The total T&M work included in this Change Order is $28,137.76. Including Change Order
Nos. 1 and 2, the revised Contract total is $968,870.98. The additional work is necessary

DISCUSSION: Change Order No. 1 includes six items associated with Bid Schedule A

Item 1A.1 is to increase Bid Item No. 2 by 3,500 square feet. The increase results in an
increase of $55,125 to the Contract.

Item 1A.2 is to increase Bid Item No. 3 by 4,000 square feet. The increase results in an
increase of $42,000 to the Contract.

Item 1A.3 is to increase the Contract time by 45 calendar days to allow for additional
work to be completed prior to winter.

Item 1B.1 is to increase Bid Item No. 7 by 500 square feet. The increase results in an
increase of $7,000 to the Contract.

Item 1B.2 is to increase Bid Item No. 8 by 1,000 square feet. The increase results in an
increase of $10,250 to the Contract.

Item 1B.3 is to increase Bid Item No. 9 by 2,000 square feet. The increase results in an
increase of $18,500 to the Contract.

Staff recommends approving Change Order No. 1 for $132,875 for both work
completed and anticipated work which will increase the Contract amount from
$332,175 to $465,050. The Change Order will also add 45 days to the Contract,
increasing it from 168 calendar days to 213 calendar days.
